source_text:
Συνεχάρην ὑμῖν μεγάλως ἐν τῷ κυρίῳ ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ, δεξαμένοις τὰ μιμήματα τῆς ἀληθοῦς ἀγάπης καὶ προπέμψασιν, ὡς ἐπέβαλεν ὑμῖν, τοὺς ἐνειλημένους τοῖς ἁγιοπρεπέσιν δεσμοῖς, ἅτινά ἐστιν διαδήματα τῶν ἀληθῶς ὑπὸ θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν ἐκλελεγμένων:
καὶ ὅτι ἡ βεβαία τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν ῥίζα, ἐξ ἀρχαίων καταγγελλομένη χρόνων, μέχρι νῦν διαμένει καὶ καρποφορεῖ εἰς τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, ὃς ὑπέμεινεν ὑπὲρ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν ἕως θανάτου καταντῆσαι, ὃν ἤγειρεν ὁ θεός, λύσας τὰς ὠδῖνας τοῦ ᾅδου:
εἰς ὃν οὐκ ἰδόντες πιστεύετε χαρᾷ ἀνεκλαλήτῳ καὶ δεδοξασμένῃ, εἰς ἣν πολλοὶ ἐπιθυμοῦσιν εἰσελθεῖν, εἰδότες, ὅτι χάριτί ἐστε σεσωσμένοι, οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων, ἀλλὰ θελήματι θεοῦ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
thought_title: Joy at the Philippians' welcome of the martyrs and their enduring faith
orientation: Polycarp opens the letter by rejoicing over the Philippians' reception of Ignatius and his fellow prisoners and over their faith, which has lasted from ancient times and now bears fruit in Christ.
pass_a_gloss: I rejoiced with you greatly in our Lord Jesus Christ, because you received the imitators of true love and sent on their way, as it was incumbent upon you, those bound in bonds fitting for the saints, which are diadems of those truly chosen by God and our Lord; and because the firm root of your faith, proclaimed from ancient times, remains until now and bears fruit unto our Lord Jesus Christ, who endured for our sins to arrive even unto death, whom God raised, having loosed the pangs of Hades; in whom, not having seen, you believe with joy inexpressible and glorified, into which many desire to enter, knowing that by grace you have been saved, not from works, but by the will of God through Jesus Christ.

choices.why: The noun means 'imitations' or 'copies,' but in context it refers to persons who imitate true love, so 'imitators' captures the personal reference.
The adjective means 'befitting holy persons'; 'holy-fitting' keeps the compound sense without smoothing it into 'holy bonds,' which would lose the nuance.
The phrase echoes Acts 2:24; 'pangs' preserves the birth-pain metaphor of ὠδῖνες, and 'Hades' keeps the Greek underworld term rather than 'death.'
The two adjectives modify 'joy'; 'inexpressible' is the standard rendering of ἀνεκλάλητος, and 'glorified' keeps the perfect passive participle force of δεδοξασμένῃ.
rejected: joy unspeakable and full of glory

choices.english: by grace you have been saved
choices.why: The dative χάριτί is instrumental, and the periphrastic perfect σεσωσμένοι ἐστε is a state resulting from past action; 'by grace you have been saved' matches Ephesians 2:5, 8.

bible_refs.note: χάριτί ἐστε σεσωσμένοι, οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων
οὐκ ἰδόντες πιστεύετε χαρᾷ ἀνεκλαλήτῳ καὶ δεδοξασμένῃ

pass_b_english: I rejoiced greatly with you in our Lord Jesus Christ. You received the examples of true love and sent them on their way, as was your duty. They were bound in chains fitting for the saints, chains that are diadems for those truly chosen by God and our Lord.

I also rejoiced because the firm root of your faith, proclaimed from ancient times, remains to this day and bears fruit for our Lord Jesus Christ. He endured for our sins even to the point of death, and God raised him, loosing the pangs of Hades.

Though you have not seen him, you believe in him with joy inexpressible and glorified, a joy many long to enter. You know that by grace you have been saved, not by works, but by the will of God through Jesus Christ.

problems.why: μιμήματα means 'examples/patterns,' not 'imitators' (people); the bonds are examples of love.
problems.ruling: μιμήματα means 'imitations/examples,' not 'imitators' (people); changes meaning from patterns of love to persons.

fixed: Changed 'imitators of true love' to 'examples of true love' because μιμήματα refers to examples or patterns, not people who imitate.

problems.quote: bound as they were in holy-fitting bonds
problems.why: 'Holy-fitting' is not natural English; reads like a calque of a Greek compound.
problems.fix: Translate as 'bonds that are fitting for the saints' or 'sacred bonds.'

edits.old: bound as they were in holy-fitting bonds—bonds that are diadems
edits.new: bound as they were in bonds fitting for the saints—bonds that are diadems

fixed: Changed 'holy-fitting bonds' to 'bonds fitting for the saints' to render the Greek compound naturally.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'endurance' not 'patient endurance' etc. Wait—checking: 'ἁγιοπρεπέσιν' not in glossary. But 'δεσμοῖς' is bonds. 'holy-fitting' is awkward but not glossary-banned. Actually: 'μιμήματα' = 'examples'—glossary has 'ὑπογραμμός' = 'example', but 'μιμήματα' is different word. No glossary issue. Re-checking: 'love of money' not here. 'righteousness' not here. No glossary errors found.
last_rejected.ruling: Checker found no actual glossary violation. 'μιμήματα' as 'examples' and 'ἁγιοπρεπέσιν' as 'holy-fitting' are within normal range; no confirmed error.

polish.changed: Broke long sentences into shorter, clearer units; clarified that the chains are the diadems; made the subject of each clause explicit; removed the em dash; kept every claim and Scripture reference intact.
